note: Review of the 48 passages that rank.py --review-out handed to review: the first eight passing passages of each claim, i.e. the 20 shown non-frozen passages, the 13 non-frozen ready replacements at positions 6 to 8, and all 15 frozen ones as a spot-check. PDFs read from .cache/ingest, SHA-256 e65882af9c9a9861b520268f739baadba08f6225feb14489ff7c46442de26ce9 (Vol 1 Rev C) and 2bf853a84de99ce4a14f8a8b58c7566068826e7d399f7ed284507e743f6e7155 (Vol 2 Rev F), equal to the snapshots, with pdfminer.six directly, not through the ingest parsers. 'Verbatim on p. N' means: the statement occurs contiguously in the text of PDF page N (or N and N+1) after whitespace normalisation and joining line-break hyphens, with the running header and 'N of M' footer removed; the section number, title and tag directly precede it; '[Rationale:' or the next numbered heading directly follows it; the tag occurs once on page N; and it contains no private-use, U+FFFD or unmapped glyph. The verdict judges the text only. 'Reviewer' judges the passage against the claim and never changes the verdict: a passage that weakens a claim stays shown.

passages.reviewer: Claude Code review agent (team Isaac Clarke)
passages.note: Shown #2. Verbatim at the top of p. 102, under heading "6.6.2.2 Individual Noise Exposure Monitoring". Reviewer: weakens the claim: "Noise exposure levels shall be monitored and quantified for each crewmember as needed for crew health and safety." Quantifying exposure per crewmember points to a personal dosimeter, which a reader may take for a body-worn device ("As an example, periodically on ISS, the crew uses acoustic monitors to monitor their environment."). It names no device, so the claim stays literally true.

Reviewer: contradicts 'No data storage' as worded: "For each isolatable, habitable compartment, the system shall automatically record pressure, humidity, temperature, ppO2, and ppCO2 data during crewed operations." The rationale adds "Additionally, the ability to view past recorded data helps to prevent environmental conditions that could harm the crew or vehicle and can aid in the effort to troubleshoot problems." It sets no capacity, retention period or log duration: "during crewed operations" says when to record, not how long to keep.

passages.note: Frozen; spot-check. Shown #2. Verbatim on p. 63, under heading "6.2.6.5 Celestial Dust Monitoring and Alerting". Reviewer: weakens the claim: "The vehicle shall monitor celestial dust and alert the crew locally and remotely when they are approaching defined limits." The limits are numbers in Vol 2 itself, not left to the program: its rationale cites "[V2 6053] Lunar Dust Contamination and [V2 6253] Martian Dust Contamination", time-weighted averages of 0.3 and 0.1 mg/m3 (p. 65). Only the alert margin ('approaching') is left open: the claim holds for crew physiology, not for crew health in general.

Reviewer: weakens mildly: "The system shall monitor trace volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in the cabin atmosphere and alert the crew locally and remotely when they are approaching defined limits." The statement sets no number, but its rationale (pp. 61-62) ties the limits to NASA's SMACs or to partner agreements: "Accepted limits may be based on JSC-20584, Spacecraft Maximum Allowable Concentrations (SMACs), or on agreements from international partners."
